card.name: Mixing or co-administering with other drugs
card.fires_on: The word "or" (sometimes "administer", "used", "given") right after "with", "mixed with", or "prior to" in sentences about giving a drug together with, or alongside, other drugs.

modes.label: "or" after with/prior to
modes.description: The word "or" joins two options such as "with, or immediately following" or "prior to or after" another drug.
modes.example: Ceftriaxone for injection solutions should not be physically mixed with<< or>> piggybacked into solutions containing other

modes.label: Verb of giving in co-use
modes.description: A verb such as administer, used, given or administered that comes before "with" or "in combination with" another product.
modes.example: Ephedrine may reduce the onset time of neuromuscular blockade when<< used>> for intubation with rocuronium

card.writes: It seems to push toward words about other drugs, competing items or concurrent use, and away from unrelated code-like pieces.
card.plain: It fires on small words in sentences about giving a drug together with, or mixing it with, another drug.
